solutions.latex:
The total number of comments is the sum of the four members' comments.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 1.29 + 2.45 + 1.46 + 2.80 \\ &= 8 \text{ million} \end{aligned}$$
The comments not for Amelia are the total minus Amelia's $2.80$ million.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{not Amelia}) &= \dfrac{8 - 2.80}{8} \\ &= \dfrac{5.2}{8} \\ &= 0.65 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the correct option is C.

The probability of a lemon tree bearing fruit in its' first season is $20\%$. Nigella plants two lemon trees.

\exfigure{496_q27_1}

figures.cap: partly completed probability tree for two lemon trees

parts.latex: Complete the probability tree diagram above to show the possible outcomes (fruit or no fruit) for the two trees.
Find the probability that neither of the trees bear fruit.
Calculate the probability that at least one of the trees will bear fruit.

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Both trees fail to bear fruit, with $P(\text{no fruit}) = 0.8$ each.
$$\begin{aligned} P(NN) &= 0.8 \times 0.8 \\ &= 0.64 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
At least one is the complement of neither.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{at least one}) &= 1 - P(\text{neither}) \\ &= 1 - 0.64 \\ &= 0.36 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

6290.stem: Ryan is playing with a well-shuffled standard deck of 52 cards.

parts.latex: What is the probability of drawing either a 4 or a black card?
What is the probability of not drawing an ace card?

solutions.latex:
There are $26$ black cards, plus the $2$ red 4's.

$$\begin{aligned} P(E) &= \dfrac{28}{52} \\ &= \dfrac{7}{13} \end{aligned}$$

figures.cap: birds on and beside a barrel

solutions.latex:
Two different birds feed, so the second bird is chosen without replacement. There are 10 birds in total.

Use the complement: "at least one yellow" is the opposite of "both blue".
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{both blue}) &= \dfrac{4}{10}\times\dfrac{3}{9} = \dfrac{2}{15} \\ P(\text{at least one yellow}) &= 1 - \dfrac{2}{15} \\ &= \dfrac{13}{15} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(\text{at least one yellow}) = \dfrac{13}{15}$$

meta.generated_note: Generated solution; assumes two different birds (no replacement).

7442.stem:
The probability tree diagram below shows the probabilities for Jack choosing a colour combination for his T-shirt and shorts. The diagram includes all the T-shirts and all the shorts that he owns.

\exfigure{264_q30_1}

figures.cap: probability tree: T-shirt colour then shorts colour

parts.latex:
The probability for white T-shirts has been left off the diagram.

Give this probability as a fraction.
What is the probability that he will choose a T-shirt and shorts that are both black?
What is the probability that he will choose a T-shirt and shorts that are the same colour?
What is the probability that he will choose a T-shirt and shorts that are different colours?

solutions.latex:
The probabilities on the first set of branches add to $1$.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{White}) &= 1-\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{3} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{6} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(\text{White T-shirt})=\dfrac{1}{6}$$

Multiply along the branches Black T-shirt, then Black shorts.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{Black, Black}) &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{5} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{10} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P=\dfrac{1}{10}$$

The same colour means Black and Black, or Blue and Blue. There are no white shorts, so White and White is not possible.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{same}) &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{1}{3}\times\dfrac{4}{5} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{10}+\dfrac{4}{15} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{30}+\dfrac{8}{30} \\ &= \dfrac{11}{30} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(\text{same colour})=\dfrac{11}{30}$$

Different colours is the complement of the same colour.
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{different}) &= 1-\dfrac{11}{30} \\ &= \dfrac{19}{30} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(\text{different colours})=\dfrac{19}{30}$$

meta.self_check: Checked by adding the six outcome probabilities: 1/10+4/10... total 1 with 11/30 same.
